summary: A proposal to add PUSH and PULL to the File Transfer Protocol as synonyms for the confusingly named STOR and RETR commands. The author argues that store and retrieve each sound ambiguous when addressed to a server.

plainLanguage.summary: The words for putting and getting a file were confusing, so someone proposed clearer words, push and pull.

subtitle: A proposal to rename confusing FTP commands with clearer synonyms.

tldr.problem: The FTP commands STOR and RETR have confusing names: telling a server to "store" or "retrieve" does not clearly indicate whether data goes in or out.
tldr.mechanism: Add PUSH and PULL as synonyms for RETR and STOR respectively, making it immediately clear which direction data flows.
tldr.outcome: The specific synonyms were not adopted, but the proposal highlighted usability issues in protocol naming.

today: While FTP did not adopt these specific synonyms, the concern about command clarity influenced later protocol design. Modern APIs and RFCs generally emphasize clear, intuitive names. The principle of supporting synonyms for backward compatibility while improving usability for new users remains sound.

sections.title: The Naming Problem
sections.content: FTP defines STOR to tell the server to accept a file (take it in) and RETR to tell the server to send a file (send it out). The trouble is that "retrieve" sounds like taking in, not sending out, and "store" could mean either direction. The names are both connotatively ambiguous and unintuitive.
sections.plainLanguage: Telling a server to "retrieve" a file sounds backwards—like the server gets it, not sends it. The names are confusing.

sections.title: The Solution
sections.content:
The proposal suggests adding PUSH and PULL as synonyms. PUSH would mean "send this to me" (RETR), and PULL would mean "take this from me" (STOR). Even GIVE and TAKE would be clearer than the existing names. At a minimum, SEND should be a synonym for RETR.

The author emphasizes adding synonyms rather than replacing the existing commands, so that existing software and user habits are not disrupted while newcomers benefit from clearer names.
sections.plainLanguage: PUSH means send me the file, PULL means take the file from me. Much clearer.

sections.title: Impact and Adoption
sections.content: The proposal raises a key point about protocol design: command names matter for usability. While FTP eventually settled on STOR and RETR as the standard, many later protocols and APIs adopted the principle of using clear, intuitive names.
sections.plainLanguage: The idea was not adopted, but it made people think about whether protocol words should be easy to remember.

references.text: Padlipsky, M.A. "FTP Command-Naming Problem", RFC 506, June 1973.
